objective: Repair the exact rejected sidecar presence-control candidate so readiness, overflow, lifecycle writes, and shutdown remain deterministic without changing the public control contract.
closed_decisions: Keep authenticated bounded JSONL control protocol v2 and every existing typed payload, size, sequence, checkpoint, reset, and reconnect-cleanup invariant.
Preserve coop/crates/coop-sidecar/src/control.rs exactly at SHA-256 8cdc427060af9159e2c563e396483ccbed2ef1e7bb1f70ec020b622d297f3179; the correction is confined to server.rs.
Stamp lifecycle commands at receipt with a readiness generation, invalidate pre-ready and prior-generation records atomically, and recheck the stamp before allocating the outer bridge sequence.
Publish mailbox overflow through an independently wakeable non-reconnectable terminal cause so channel EOF cannot obscure PresenceQueueFull.
Only a confirmed reboot branch may arm the sticky lifecycle-forwarding disable latch; a legitimate initial active-epoch ROM_READY must retain forwarding.

Use one non-cancellable sole bridge-writer path or equivalent frame-safe ownership so lifecycle traffic cannot block the critical shutdown lane beyond its 500 ms acknowledgement bound; failed or partial writes close the bridge and it is never reused.
Do not reconnect, remint, retry lifecycle records, or restart realtime after reset, lifecycle-terminal, overflow, or control ambiguity in one authenticated session.
forbidden_changes: Do not edit control.rs, launcher, protocol, realtime-core, cloud, server-service, ROM, Lua, Cargo, documentation, generated artifacts, or orchestration files.
Do not weaken authentication, the 512-byte LF-inclusive JSONL bound, epoch or sequence validation, checkpoint semantics, shutdown reservation, error redaction, or reconnect cleanup.
Do not add credentials, endpoint data, generic serde_json::Value, arbitrary bytes, unbounded queues, silent lifecycle loss, cancelled partial bridge frames, or a second bridge writer.
Do not stage, commit, branch, fetch, pull, push, contact remotes, create or remove worktrees, or revert any other worker's edits; preserve the sealed index and all unowned content.

acceptance_criteria.description: A legitimate initial active-epoch ROM_READY cannot disable lifecycle forwarding; only a confirmed reboot arms the sticky latch, and a real serving-loop regression proves a subsequent lifecycle command is forwarded.
Capacity overflow wakes the real serving loop through a stable terminal path and deterministically returns PresenceQueueFull before reconnectable EOF can win.

A deterministically stalled lifecycle bridge write cannot delay a correlated authenticated shutdown Applied result beyond the 500 ms launcher bound, while sole-writer ownership and complete bridge-frame integrity remain fail-closed.
A lifecycle command received before readiness cannot later forward after bridge authentication, cannot consume an outer sequence, and a fresh post-ready command does forward.
Existing authenticated protocol, payload, sequence, checkpoint, reset, reboot, and reconnect-cleanup invariants remain unchanged.

Focused real-serving-path regressions, the full sidecar suite, strict Clippy, formatting, and diff checks pass; the root-observed implementation delta contains only server.rs and control.rs remains byte-identical.

return_when: Every acceptance criterion is resolved and every required command outcome is recorded.
A safe correction requires changing a forbidden public or cross-unit boundary.
A concrete toolchain failure prevents further progress within the execution budget.
